title: Improving write performance on SQL Server
question:
I have a few million rows of data that needs to be transferred into another SQL Server DB and was testing the speed with a small number of rows.

Using the JDBC driver the best speed was 44 rows/s. Then I switched to the SQL Spark connector which sped up the process significantly to 333 rows/s. But this is still very slow and needed to know what I could do to increase the speed.

This is my code

df.write.format("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.spark")\
.mode("overwrite")\
.option("driver", driver2)\
.option("url", url2)\
.option("dbtable", table)\
.option("user", user2)\
.option("password", password2)\
.option("batchsize",batchsize)\
.option("reliabilityLevel","BEST_EFFORT")\
.save()

I'm running this on my local pc with 1 executor, 8 cores.
I have partitioned my dataframe into 8.
Using Spark v3.1.3 (for the sql connector)

I have tried changing the batch sizes and number of partitions, not sure if I'm tuning them correctly but have done a lot of trial and error. When looking for ways to optimize I saw that people had an extremely fast speed for writing even before they optimized their code. So I'm not sure what the problem is anymore.

Using Pyspark is a requirement and at a later stage I would be live-streaming the data from multiple nodes. I am currently testing on my local system to familiarize myself with the works. If there's a solution specific to the later stages that's different than when I do it locally, then please let me know.
answer:
It depends on the load and server capacity and properties. But if i were you if possible i prefer to use a heap table to load. Indexes can be slowing down to write operations. Bulk copy is a good approach to load big data. (SqlBulkCopy (C#), or BULK INSERT on SQLServer)

If you prefer you have a primary key best practice then at least except the primary key do not add any indexes. You will be getting better performance for this.
